questions.text: In which year was the United Nations founded?
questions.explanation: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945 after the Second World War, replacing the League of Nations.

questions.text: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters complex is in New York City, on land donated by John D. Rockefeller Jr.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
questions.explanation: The five permanent UNSC members are the US, UK, France, Russia and China; Germany has never held a permanent seat.

questions.text: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: Trygve Lie of Norway served as the first UN Secretary-General, from 1946 to 1952.

questions.text: In which year was the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) established?
questions.explanation: NATO was founded on 4 April 1949 with the signing of the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, D.C.

questions.text: The headquarters of NATO is located in which city?
questions.explanation: NATO's headquarters has been located in Brussels, Belgium, since 1967.

questions.text: How many countries signed the original North Atlantic Treaty in 1949?
questions.explanation: Twelve countries, including the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, were the founding members of NATO in 1949.

questions.text: The European Union was formally established by which treaty?
questions.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty, signed in 1992 and effective from November 1993, created the European Union.

questions.text: In which year was the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) founded?
questions.explanation: ASEAN was founded on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok.

questions.text: How many countries were founding members of ASEAN in 1967?
questions.explanation: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand were the five founding members of ASEAN.

questions.text: The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established in which year?
questions.explanation: SAARC was founded in 1985 with the signing of its charter in Dhaka.

questions.text: The permanent secretariat of SAARC is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat has been headquartered in Kathmandu, Nepal, since 1987.

questions.text: In which year was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) founded?
questions.explanation: The OIC (originally the Organisation of the Islamic Conference) was founded in 1969 following an emergency summit in Rabat.

questions.text: The headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The OIC's headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, though it was intended to move to Jerusalem once liberated.

questions.text: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the G7?
questions.explanation: The G7 comprises the US, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and Canada; China is not a member.

questions.text: The 1955 Bandung Conference of Asian and African nations was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: The Bandung Conference, a landmark meeting of newly independent Asian and African states, was held in Bandung, Indonesia, in April 1955.

questions.text: The 1978 Camp David Accords led to a peace treaty between which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Camp David Accords, brokered by US President Jimmy Carter, led to the 1979 Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty.

questions.text: The Kyoto Protocol, an international treaty committing states to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, was adopted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in Kyoto, Japan, in December 1997 and entered into force in 2005.

questions.text: The Paris Agreement on climate change was adopted at which UN climate conference?
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21, held in Paris in December 2015.

questions.text: The 2021 UN Climate Change Conference (COP26) was held in which city?
questions.explanation: COP26 was hosted by the United Kingdom in Glasgow, Scotland, in November 2021.

questions.text: The 2022 UN Climate Change Conference (COP27) was held in which country?
questions.explanation: COP27 was held in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, in November 2022.

questions.text: The 2023 UN Climate Change Conference (COP28) was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: COP28 was held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, in November-December 2023.

questions.text: The 2024 UN Climate Change Conference (COP29) was held in which city?
questions.explanation: COP29 was hosted in Baku, Azerbaijan, in November 2024.

questions.text: The 2025 UN Climate Change Conference (COP30) was hosted in which Brazilian city?
questions.explanation: COP30 was held in Belem, a city on the edge of the Amazon basin, in November 2025.

questions.text: The 2020 Abraham Accords normalised relations between Israel and which two Arab states?
questions.explanation: The Abraham Accords, brokered by the US in 2020, saw the UAE and Bahrain establish formal diplomatic relations with Israel.

questions.text: The 'S' was added to BRIC to form 'BRICS' in 2010 when which country joined the grouping?
questions.explanation: South Africa joined the original BRIC bloc (Brazil, Russia, India, China) in 2010, forming BRICS.

questions.text: Which of the following countries formally joined BRICS as a new member on 1 January 2024?
questions.explanation: Egypt, along with Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE, formally joined BRICS on 1 January 2024, expanding the bloc.

questions.text: The G20 summit of 2022 was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: Indonesia hosted the 2022 G20 summit in Bali.

questions.text: The G20 summit of 2023 was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: India hosted the 2023 G20 summit in New Delhi.

questions.text: The G20 summit of 2024 was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: Brazil hosted the 2024 G20 summit in Rio de Janeiro.

questions.text: The 2025 G20 summit, the first ever held on the African continent, was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: South Africa hosted the 2025 G20 summit in Johannesburg, the first G20 summit held in Africa.

questions.text: The treaty that formally ended the First World War between Germany and the Allied Powers was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919, formally ending the First World War.

questions.text: The 1944 Bretton Woods Conference led to the creation of which two international financial institutions?
questions.explanation: The Bretton Woods Conference established the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank).

questions.text: The World Health Organization, founded in 1948, has its headquarters in which city?
questions.explanation: The WHO was established in 1948 and is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.text: UNESCO, the UN's cultural and educational agency, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: UNESCO was founded in 1945 and is headquartered in Paris, France.

questions.text: Unlike the other Nobel Prizes, the Nobel Peace Prize is awarded each year in which city?
questions.explanation: While other Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm, the Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway, per Alfred Nobel's will.

questions.text: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, sits in which city?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice is seated at the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.text: The Schengen Agreement, which abolished internal border checks among most European states, was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Schengen Agreement was signed in 1985 near the town of Schengen, Luxembourg.

questions.text: The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), the Iran nuclear deal, was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The JCPOA was signed in July 2015 between Iran and the P5+1 group of world powers.

questions.text: AUKUS, a trilateral security partnership announced in 2021, involves Australia, the United Kingdom and which other country?
questions.explanation: AUKUS is a security pact between Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States, announced in September 2021.

questions.text: The Berlin Wall, which divided East and West Berlin, fell in which year?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989, paving the way for German reunification in 1990.

questions.text: The Soviet Union formally dissolved in which year?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union was formally dissolved on 26 December 1991.

questions.text: The concept of the modern sovereign nation-state is commonly traced to which 1648 treaty?
questions.explanation: The Peace of Westphalia in 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War and established the principle of state sovereignty.

questions.text: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), founded in 1960, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960 and has been headquartered in Vienna, Austria, since 1965.

questions.text: The first FIFA World Cup, held in 1930, was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: Uruguay hosted and won the inaugural FIFA World Cup in 1930.

questions.text: The 1950 FIFA World Cup was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: Brazil hosted the 1950 FIFA World Cup, famously losing the deciding match to Uruguay at the Maracana.

questions.text: Which country won the 1950 FIFA World Cup, held in Brazil, in the famous 'Maracanazo' upset?
questions.explanation: Uruguay defeated the host nation Brazil in the deciding match to win the 1950 World Cup.

questions.text: England won its only FIFA World Cup title as host nation in which year?
questions.explanation: England won the 1966 FIFA World Cup, which it also hosted, defeating West Germany in the final.

questions.text: Brazil won its third FIFA World Cup title at the 1970 tournament held in which country?
questions.explanation: Brazil won the 1970 World Cup in Mexico, becoming the first team to win the title three times.

questions.text: The 1974 FIFA World Cup was won by the host nation, which was:
questions.explanation: West Germany hosted and won the 1974 FIFA World Cup, defeating the Netherlands in the final.

questions.text: Argentina won its first FIFA World Cup title as host nation in which year?
questions.explanation: Argentina hosted and won the 1978 FIFA World Cup.

questions.text: The 1986 FIFA World Cup, famous for Diego Maradona's 'Hand of God' goal, was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: Mexico hosted the 1986 World Cup, which Argentina won under the captaincy of Diego Maradona.

questions.text: The 1990 FIFA World Cup, won by West Germany, was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: Italy hosted the 1990 FIFA World Cup, which West Germany won for a third time.

questions.text: The 1994 FIFA World Cup, the first held in the United States, was won by which country?
questions.explanation: Brazil won the 1994 World Cup, held in the United States, beating Italy on penalties in the final.

questions.text: France won its first FIFA World Cup title as host nation in which year?
questions.explanation: France hosted and won the 1998 FIFA World Cup, defeating Brazil in the final.

questions.text: The 2002 FIFA World Cup, the first held in Asia, was jointly hosted by which two countries?
questions.explanation: Japan and South Korea co-hosted the 2002 FIFA World Cup, the first tournament held in Asia and the first co-hosted edition.

questions.text: The 2006 FIFA World Cup, hosted by Germany, was won by which country?
questions.explanation: Italy won the 2006 FIFA World Cup in Germany, defeating France on penalties in the final.

questions.text: The 2010 FIFA World Cup, the first held on the African continent, was won by which country?
questions.explanation: Spain won its first World Cup title at the 2010 tournament hosted by South Africa.

questions.text: The 2014 FIFA World Cup, hosted by Brazil, was won by which country?
questions.explanation: Germany won the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, defeating Argentina in the final.

questions.text: The 2018 FIFA World Cup, hosted by Russia, was won by which country?
questions.explanation: France won the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia, defeating Croatia in the final.

questions.text: The 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first held in the Middle East, was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first World Cup held in the Middle East; Argentina won the title.

questions.text: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be the first ever jointly hosted by three countries. Which three?
questions.explanation: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be co-hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico, the first edition hosted by three nations.

questions.text: FIFA, football's global governing body, was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: FIFA was founded in Paris in 1904 but has been headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, since 1932.

questions.text: As of the 2022 tournament, which country has won the most FIFA World Cup titles?
questions.explanation: Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup a record five times: 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002.

questions.text: The first modern Olympic Games were held in 1896 in which city?
questions.explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

questions.text: The modern Olympic Games were revived in the 19th century largely due to the efforts of which Frenchman?
questions.explanation: Pierre de Coubertin founded the International Olympic Committee and is credited with reviving the modern Olympic Games.

questions.text: The International Olympic Committee, founded in 1894, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The IOC was founded in 1894 and is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

questions.text: Many Western countries, led by the United States, boycotted the 1980 Summer Olympics held in which city, in protest at the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: The US led a boycott of the 1980 Moscow Olympics after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in 1979.

questions.text: The 2008 Summer Olympics were hosted by which city?
questions.explanation: Beijing hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics, its first as an Olympic host city.

questions.text: London became the first city to host the Summer Olympics three times when it hosted the Games in which year?
questions.explanation: London hosted the Summer Olympics in 1908, 1948, and 2012, becoming the first three-time host city.

questions.text: The 2016 Summer Olympics, the first held in South America, were hosted by which city?
questions.explanation: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics, the first Games held in South America.

questions.text: The 2020 Summer Olympics, hosted by Tokyo, were actually held in which year due to the COVID-19 pandemic?
questions.explanation: The Tokyo Olympics, officially the 2020 Games, were postponed and held in the summer of 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

questions.text: Beijing became the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Olympics when it hosted the Winter Games in which year?
questions.explanation: Beijing hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics, having also hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics, making it the first city to host both.

questions.text: The 2024 Summer Olympics were hosted by which city, hosting the Games for a third time?
questions.explanation: Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics, having previously hosted in 1900 and 1924.

questions.text: The 2026 Winter Olympics are being co-hosted by Milan and which other Italian town?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Winter Olympics are jointly hosted by Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo in northern Italy.

questions.text: The first Winter Olympic Games were held in 1924 in which town?
questions.explanation: The first Winter Olympics were held in Chamonix, France, in 1924.

questions.text: What is the traditional Olympic motto, in Latin?
questions.explanation: 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' (Faster, Higher, Stronger) has been the Olympic motto since 1894.

questions.text: The five interlocking rings of the Olympic flag represent:
questions.explanation: The five Olympic rings symbolise the union of the five inhabited continents participating in the Games.

questions.text: The first Cricket World Cup, held in 1975, was won by which team?
questions.explanation: The West Indies won the inaugural Cricket World Cup, held in England in 1975.

questions.text: India won its first Cricket World Cup title in which year, defeating West Indies in the final?
questions.explanation: India won the 1983 Cricket World Cup, defeating the two-time defending champions West Indies in the final at Lord's.

questions.text: Pakistan won its only Cricket World Cup title in 1992, a tournament co-hosted by which two countries?
questions.explanation: Pakistan, captained by Imran Khan, won the 1992 Cricket World Cup, co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand.

questions.text: Sri Lanka won its only Cricket World Cup title in which year?
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka won the 1996 Cricket World Cup, held on the subcontinent, defeating Australia in the final.

questions.text: The 1999 Cricket World Cup, hosted by England, was won by which team?
questions.explanation: Australia won the 1999 Cricket World Cup, defeating Pakistan in the final at Lord's.

questions.text: India won its second Cricket World Cup title in 2011, a tournament it co-hosted with which countries?
questions.explanation: India co-hosted the 2011 Cricket World Cup with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, and won the title on home soil.

questions.text: England won its first Cricket World Cup title in 2019 in a final decided by a Super Over against which team?
questions.explanation: England won the 2019 Cricket World Cup final against New Zealand, which was tied and decided by a Super Over.

questions.text: The 2023 Cricket World Cup, hosted by India, was won by which country for a record sixth time?
questions.explanation: Australia defeated host nation India in the final to win a record sixth Cricket World Cup title in 2023.

questions.text: The International Cricket Council was originally founded in 1909 under which name?
questions.explanation: The ICC began in 1909 as the Imperial Cricket Conference, comprising England, Australia and South Africa, before being renamed in 1965 and again in 1989.

questions.text: Sputnik 1, the world's first artificial satellite, was launched in 1957 by which country?
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957, starting the Space Age.

questions.text: Who became the first human to journey into outer space, in 1961?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961, becoming the first human in space.

questions.text: The first crewed Moon landing was achieved by which mission in 1969?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed the first humans on the Moon on 20 July 1969.

questions.text: Who was the first person to walk on the surface of the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface first during the Apollo 11 mission on 20 July 1969.

questions.text: NASA, the US space agency, was established in which year?
questions.explanation: NASA was created in 1958, largely in response to the Soviet launch of Sputnik.

questions.text: The Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 space probes, which studied the outer planets, were launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Both Voyager probes were launched in 1977 and have since travelled beyond the outer planets into interstellar space.

questions.text: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched into orbit in which year?
questions.explanation: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery in April 1990.

questions.text: The first module of the International Space Station was launched in which year?
questions.explanation: The ISS's first module, Zarya, was launched in November 1998, beginning assembly of the station in orbit.

questions.text: NASA's Curiosity rover landed on Mars in which year?
questions.explanation: The Curiosity rover landed in Gale Crater on Mars in August 2012.

questions.text: NASA's Perseverance rover, which carried the Ingenuity helicopter, landed on Mars in which year?
questions.explanation: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater on Mars in February 2021.

questions.text: In August 2023, India's Chandrayaan-3 mission achieved which milestone?
options: First soft landing near the Moon's south pole
First sample return from an asteroid
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land near the Moon's south pole and the fourth to achieve a soft lunar landing, in August 2023.

questions.text: NASA's Artemis I mission, an uncrewed test flight of the Orion spacecraft around the Moon, launched in which year?
questions.explanation: Artemis I launched in November 2022, testing the Space Launch System rocket and Orion capsule ahead of future crewed Moon missions.

questions.text: The James Webb Space Telescope, the successor to Hubble, was launched in which month and year?
questions.explanation: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched on 25 December 2021.

questions.text: The first-ever direct image of a black hole was released in which year?
questions.explanation: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released the first image of a black hole, at the centre of galaxy M87, in April 2019.

questions.text: Gravitational waves, predicted by Einstein a century earlier, were first directly detected in which year?
questions.explanation: The LIGO observatories made the first direct detection of gravitational waves in September 2015, announced in February 2016.

questions.text: The Higgs boson particle was experimentally confirmed in 2012 at which research facility?
questions.explanation: The Higgs boson was discovered at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012, confirming a particle theorised in 1964.

questions.text: CERN, the European Organization for Nuclear Research, was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: CERN was established in 1954 and operates the Large Hadron Collider near Geneva.

questions.text: India's Chandrayaan-1 mission, launched in 2008, is credited with helping confirm the presence of what on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Data from Chandrayaan-1, launched in 2008, provided key evidence of water molecules on the lunar surface.

questions.text: India's Mars Orbiter Mission ('Mangalyaan') successfully entered Mars orbit in which year, making India the first Asian country to reach Mars?
questions.explanation: Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit in September 2014, making ISRO the first Asian space agency to do so.

questions.text: China's Chang'e 4 mission achieved the first-ever soft landing on which part of the Moon, in January 2019?
questions.explanation: Chang'e 4 became the first spacecraft to land on the far side of the Moon, in January 2019.

questions.text: SpaceX achieved the first successful landing of an orbital-class rocket's first stage in which year?
questions.explanation: SpaceX first landed a Falcon 9 first stage successfully in December 2015, a milestone for reusable rockets.

questions.text: In 2020, which company launched the first crewed orbital spaceflight from US soil since the Space Shuttle era, to the ISS?
questions.explanation: SpaceX's Crew Dragon Demo-2 mission in May 2020 carried NASA astronauts to the ISS, the first crewed US orbital launch since 2011.

questions.text: Aditya-L1, launched by India in 2023, is a mission to study which celestial body?
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 is ISRO's first dedicated mission to study the Sun, launched in September 2023.

questions.text: The double-helix structure of DNA was described in 1953 by James Watson and which co-researcher?
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick published the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953, drawing on X-ray data from Rosalind Franklin.

questions.text: The Human Genome Project, which mapped nearly all human genes, was declared complete in which year?
questions.explanation: The Human Genome Project was declared essentially complete in April 2003.

questions.text: Dolly, the first mammal successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell, was born in which year?
questions.explanation: Dolly the sheep was born in 1996 at the Roslin Institute in Scotland, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

questions.text: Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was discovered by which scientist in 1928?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 after noticing mould inhibiting bacterial growth in his laboratory.

questions.text: The World Wide Web was invented in 1989 by Tim Berners-Lee while working at which institution?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN, the European particle physics laboratory.

questions.text: Apple released the first iPhone in which year?
questions.explanation: The first iPhone was released by Apple in June 2007.

questions.text: The 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded for the development of which gene-editing technology?
questions.explanation: Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing tools.

questions.text: The first COVID-19 vaccine to receive widespread emergency authorisation, in December 2020, was developed by Pfizer in partnership with which company?
questions.explanation: The Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine received emergency authorisation in December 2020, among the first in the world to do so.

questions.text: Albert Einstein published his theory of general relativity in which year?
questions.explanation: Einstein published his general theory of relativity in 1915, extending his 1905 special theory.

questions.text: The periodic table of chemical elements, arranging elements by atomic weight and properties, was devised in 1869 by which scientist?
questions.explanation: Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev published his periodic table of elements in 1869, successfully predicting undiscovered elements.

questions.text: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in which year?
questions.explanation: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901, five years after Alfred Nobel's death, per his will.

questions.text: ARPANET, the precursor to the modern internet, transmitted its first message between computers in which year?
questions.explanation: ARPANET sent its first host-to-host message in October 1969, between UCLA and Stanford Research Institute.

questions.text: Pluto, discovered in 1930, was reclassified from a planet to a 'dwarf planet' by the International Astronomical Union in which year?
questions.explanation: The IAU reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006 after defining stricter criteria for what constitutes a planet.

questions.text: The Wright brothers achieved the first sustained, controlled, powered flight of an aircraft in which year?
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright achieved the first powered flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, on 17 December 1903.

questions.text: Which 19th-century French scientist developed the process of pasteurisation and advanced the germ theory of disease?
questions.explanation: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurisation and provided key evidence for the germ theory of disease in the 19th century.

questions.text: Marie Curie was the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields. Which two?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911.

questions.text: Halley's Comet, one of the most famous periodic comets, returns to the vicinity of Earth approximately every how many years?
questions.explanation: Halley's Comet has an orbital period of roughly 76 years; it was last visible from Earth in 1986 and is expected to return around 2061.

questions.text: mRNA vaccine technology, long researched but never before approved for public use, was first deployed at scale during which event?
questions.explanation: The COVID-19 pandemic saw the first large-scale approval and rollout of mRNA vaccines, developed by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, from late 2020.

questions.text: Charles Darwin's 'On the Origin of Species', which introduced the theory of evolution by natural selection, was published in which year?
questions.explanation: Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859, setting out the theory of evolution by natural selection.

questions.text: Alexander Graham Bell was granted a patent for the telephone in which year?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for the telephone in 1876.
